hero.title: Vantage — Every action. A clearer picture.

lines.text: Somewhere tonight, a Marine is finishing work that no one will ever see.
Thirty reconciliations. A funding gap, caught in time.
By morning, most of it is gone.
Into a spreadsheet. An inbox. Somebody’s memory.
Vantage keeps it.
Say what you did, once. Vantage reads the numbers, and shows you before it saves.
Your section’s work, in one queue. Claim it, and it’s yours.
Cases follow cited procedures. Evidence before action. Resolved only when verified.
Open commitments. Undelivered orders.
Read in the order the money moves.
Every entry, signed into the history. Nothing important happens quietly.
And the credit goes to the Marine who did the work.
When evaluation season comes, the record is already written, and every line cites its source.
Leaders see the whole section at a glance.
Private by default. Built to run on your own network.
Vantage. Give good work a lasting record.

quick-log.title: Quick Log: a record in one sentence

lines.text: Quick Log.
The fastest way to keep a record. Press N, anywhere in Vantage.
Write it the way you’d say it out loud.
Vantage reads the count, the dollar value and what kind of value it is, the system, and the date.
Check what it understood, then save. It lands in your record, dated, and yours.
No signal? It waits on your device, and syncs when you’re back.
Working a case.
Work arrives as a queue your whole section can see.
Claim a case, and it’s on your list at once. Claiming isn’t credit. The work is.
The procedure shows the next step, and the form asks only for what that step needs.
Record what you found, and Vantage calculates the candidate, citing every input.
Decide, with your reason. A step that needs evidence first says so, before it refuses.
Every entry is signed into the history. Hand it on, and each of you keeps exactly what you did.
Reading a balance.
The Reference is the FMRA desk reference, inside Vantage, with every statement cited.
Enter a document’s commitment, obligation, delivered, and paid.
Vantage names the open condition, the causes worth ruling out, who can act, and what would prove the fix.
A dash on a report isn’t a zero. Mark it not shown.
Open a case, and the figures come with it, labelled with where they came from.
Your Record.
It keeps three things apart. What you hold, which isn’t credit. What you contributed, counted from the work itself. And what you logged yourself.
One document counts once, however many entries it took.
From any case you worked, prepare a private draft, built only from your own facts.
Keep it, and it lands in your record, with a link back to the case.
Report Studio.
Report Studio turns your record into JEPES or FITREP input.
Choose the period, and the entries it should cite.
Write against facts you can open and check.
Save, and the revision is locked to exactly what was reviewed.
Leading a section.
As a section lead, Today puts your section first: what’s unassigned, overdue, blocked, and waiting, and on what.
See how many open commitments, undelivered orders and UMTs you’re carrying.
Workload shows who holds what, beside what each count means.
Counts never measure effort. And zero recorded is never zero work.
Your first week.
Day one starts with an invitation from your leader. Choose a username, and a password of your own.
Today opens with a short list for the week. Each step ticks itself off as you do it.
First, protect your sign-in with a passkey or an authenticator app, so a password alone is never enough.
Check your profile. Your rank decides whether you build JEPES or FITREP input.
Then log something you did. One sentence is enough.
By Friday, open Team: who you work with, the command above you, and the goals you share.

visibility.title: Private, unit, and who can see what

lines.text: Who can see what.
Every entry has an audience, and you choose it when you save.
Only me means exactly that. No leader can open it, and neither can the instance owner.
Share it with your unit, and it counts on the unit dashboard, for leaders who can read that unit’s records.
Every entry says who can see it, in plain words, at the top.
Drafts and career plans are never shared. And every time a leader opens your record, it is logged.
Importing a spreadsheet.
Bring in the sheet your section already works from. Vantage keeps the original, unchanged.
It reads the headings, and guesses what each column means. Correct anything it got wrong.
Before anything is written, you see exactly what will happen, row by row.
Import, and every row becomes work in the queue, traced to the row it came from.
Bring the same file in again, and nothing changes. That is the right answer.
Reading the analysis.
Before you claim anything, see what your record actually shows.
Figures are grouped by what they measure. Hours, kilometres and dollars are never added together.
The summary says it plainly: how often you logged, your longest gap, and where this pace will leave you.
Coverage shows which entries are thin, so you can strengthen them before a report cites them.
And a figure on Today opens into the entries behind it.
Counseling.
From a Marine’s page, record the counseling: what went well, what to improve, and the goals you set.
Save it, and it is on their record, dated, with you as the counselor.
They open it from Career, and acknowledge it. That confirms they read it, not that they agree.
Both of you hold the same dated record, and it shows as acknowledged.
Standing up a deployment.
The first launch asks for one thing: the owner account, and the first unit you will lead.
The Owner console runs the deployment: settings, accounts, units, retention and backups.
Decide the settings before anyone else signs in, starting with whether people may register themselves.
Build the chain of command. Teams sit under their command, and authority flows down, never up.
Then bring people in: an invitation they accept themselves, or accounts imported from a roster.

governance.title: Retention, holds and the privacy inventory

lines.text: Retention and privacy.
Retention is off until you turn it on, one kind of record at a time, and every schedule names its authority.
See what is eligible before anything runs.
A legal hold stops every deletion it covers, and always wins over a schedule.
The privacy inventory is built from the live database each time it opens, so it cannot quietly stop being true.
Export it for the privacy impact assessment.
